headline: LEAKED DOCS EXPOSE BHP: World's Biggest Miner Quietly Shelved Billions in Pilbara Climate Projects
snippet: Internal documents obtained by the ABC and The Guardian reveal BHP shelved board-approved renewable energy and electrification projects at its Pilbara iron ore operations, pausing a solar-battery installation at Jimblebar and a 500MW wind-solar-battery system — even as executives publicly championed the company's climate credentials. BHP's own internal warnings noted that slow emissions cuts could damage its licence to operate across its most profitable division.

headline: GHANA ORDERS NEWMONT, ANGLOGOLD, GOLD FIELDS to Sell 30% of Output to Central Bank From June 1
snippet: Ghana's Bank of Ghana has finalised agreements with Africa's three largest gold miners — Newmont, AngloGold Ashanti, and Gold Fields — to increase mandatory doré gold sales from 20% to 30% of output, effective June 1, 2026, at a 0.6% price discount. The policy shift aims to boost the country's gold reserves, support the cedi, and channel production through Gold Coast Refinery before LBMA certification at South Africa's Rand Refinery.

headline: AZIMUT DRILLS 46.41 g/t Au OVER 3.5m — Rosa Zone Corridor Now 1.4km Strike, Open in All Directions, James Bay
snippet: Azimut Exploration (TSXV: AZM) reported best hole results of 46.41 g/t Au over 3.50m, including 155 g/t Au over 1.0m, from its second drill campaign on the Rosa gold zone at the Wabamisk Property in Quebec's James Bay region. The 20-hole program (3,018m) confirmed two subparallel gold-bearing structures over a 1.4-km strike within a 100m-wide corridor, with the zone remaining open in all directions.

headline: Gold Steady at $4,536 as Middle East Conflict and Rate-Hike Odds at 55% Box In Safe-Haven Demand
snippet: Spot gold traded at $4,536/oz on May 26, still 37% higher year-over-year, as geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East and renewed Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations created conflicting currents. Markets are now pricing a 55% probability of at least one 25bp rate hike by October, capping gold's recovery from the $4,500 floor reached last week.

headline: Golconda Gold Q1: Galaxy-Princeton Complex Produces 4,372 Tonnes Concentrate at 25.9 g/t; Summit Mine On Q2 Schedule
snippet: Golconda Gold mined 44,042 tonnes of ore at an average mill feed grade of 3.03 g/t from its Galaxy and Princeton ore bodies in Q1 2026, producing 4,372 tonnes of concentrate averaging 25.9 g/t. The company's Summit Mine in New Mexico remains on track to commence mining by end of Q2 2026.

headline: GoldMining Fires Up Drill at 1.23Moz Yarumalito Gold-Copper Project in Colombia's Mid Cauca Belt
snippet: GoldMining Inc. (TSX: GOLD) commenced a 1,200-metre systematic diamond core drill program at its 100%-owned Yarumalito gold-copper project in Colombia's Mid Cauca belt, targeting high-priority zones within an inferred resource of 1.23Moz Au and 129Mlb Cu. The program follows comprehensive relogging of historical core that identified new geological targets not previously drill-tested.

headline: COPPER SLIDES TO LOWEST SINCE MARCH at $5.50/lb as Oil-Price Shock from Middle East Conflict Weighs on Industrial Metals
snippet: Copper fell to $5.50/lb on May 26 — its weakest level since March 2026 — as escalating Middle East conflict drove oil higher, amplifying inflation concerns and dampening near-term industrial demand expectations. AI electrification demand and a structural supply deficit continue to provide an underlying floor, but macro headwinds have shifted short-term sentiment cautious.

headline: CONGO M23 REBELS Pitch Tantalum, Tin and Tungsten Directly to Trump Administration — Conflict Mineral Risks Flagged
snippet: Rwanda-backed M23 rebels controlling mineral-rich eastern Congo are seeking to sell tantalum, tin, and tungsten directly to the Trump administration, hoping Washington's push for non-Chinese critical mineral supply chains will translate into political legitimacy and economic support. Analysts warn the move risks legitimizing conflict minerals and undermining international certification systems designed to prevent supply chains from financing violence.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS NEAR $86/LB at Two-Month Highs as Meta Inks 7.8GW Nuclear Deal, Microsoft Commits 800MW
snippet: Uranium futures held above $86.5/lb on May 25, near their highest level in two months, as AI data center operators locked in nuclear supply agreements at scale. Meta signed agreements for up to 7.8 gigawatts of nuclear capacity and Microsoft committed more than 800 megawatts of renewed nuclear power exclusively for AI data center operations, reinforcing the long-term demand outlook amid a structural supply deficit.

headline: NdPr OXIDE DOWN 21% IN APRIL — But Rare Earths Still 88% Above January After Trump-Xi Summit Repricing
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg — its sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally began — pulling neodymium and praseodymium oxides to $108-$109/kg range. Despite the correction, NdPr remains 88% above its January open and well above the operational cost base of major Western producers including MP Materials and Lynas, following the Trump-Xi summit that put rare earth supply chains at the centre of strategic negotiations.
